blocks.text: Be the first player to reach 10 Victory Points to win.
The game ends immediately the moment a player reaches 10 or more points on their turn.
Some game modes change this target — Blitz is played to 6 Victory Points (see Game Modes).
The board is made of hexagonal terrain tiles, each producing a resource, plus number tokens that trigger production.
Roads and buildings are placed on the intersections and edges between tiles.
Each player picks a color and receives their roads, settlements, cities, and development cards.
In turn order, players place two starting settlements and two connected roads; both settlements must follow the Distance Rule.
After the second settlement, collect one resource card from every terrain tile touching it.
In Draft mode this bonus is replaced by the cards you drafted (see Game Modes).
Settlements and cities can never sit directly next to each other — at least one empty intersection must separate them.
This applies both during setup and to all later building.
You may trade and build as many times as you can afford during your turn.
When a tile's number is rolled, every settlement touching it produces 1 of its resource, and every city produces 2. The desert never produces.
Example: a Settlement next to a Forest numbered 6 produces 1 Lumber when a 6 is rolled — a City there produces 2.
A Season Track cycles through Spring → Summer → Autumn → Winter → Spring, each changing how resources are produced.
The season advances every 5 completed turns, or whenever a player claims Largest Army.
When a 6 or 8 is rolled during Spring, Fields and Pastures produce one extra resource on top of their normal output.
Example: a Settlement on a 6 Field normally makes 1 Grain — 2 Grain in Spring, or 3 Grain for a City.
During Summer, any tile numbered 5 or 9 produces double its normal output, for every resource type.
Example: a Settlement on a 5 Forest normally makes 1 Lumber — 2 in Summer; a City there would make 4.
During Autumn, Forests and Hills also produce on rolls of 3 and 11, in addition to their normal number.
Example: a Forest numbered 8 produces Lumber on 8, 3, and 11 — making weaker numbers valuable again.
When a 2 or 12 is rolled during Winter, normal production is skipped — instead, the robber moves to that tile.
Every player with a Settlement or City on that hex loses 1 random resource card. The robber does not steal in this case.
The current season is visible to everyone and stays active until the next trigger occurs.
If a season change and a Largest Army claim happen at the same time, the season only advances once.
Cost: 1 Lumber + 1 Brick.
A new road must connect to one of your existing roads, settlements, or cities, and can never cross through an opponent's settlement or city.
Cost: 1 Lumber + 1 Brick + 1 Grain + 1 Wool.
Must be placed on an empty intersection connected to one of your roads, and must follow the Distance Rule. Produces 1 resource from each adjacent tile.
Cost: 2 Grain + 3 Ore.
Built by upgrading one of your existing settlements — the settlement is replaced. A city produces 2 resources instead of 1 from each adjacent tile.
A unique building that lets you seize a location occupied by an opponent's city, by paying 3 Ore + 4 Lumber + 2 Wool + 1 Brick.
The opponent's city is removed and replaced by your Resort, and any Victory Points it held are lost.
A Resort can never be built on a Settlement, and once placed it cannot be overwritten or replaced.
On your turn, you may negotiate any trade with another player, as long as both sides agree and it follows the resource rules.
For example: "1 Ore for 2 Grain."
Trade 4 of one identical resource for 1 resource of your choice, at any time on your turn.
Ports can offer better rates than the standard bank trade.

items: General Port — 3 of one resource → 1 of your choice
Specialized Port — 2 of the matching resource → 1 of your choice

blocks.text: Available ports depend on the map in play.
Cost: 1 Grain + 1 Wool + 1 Ore.

items: Knight — move the robber and steal
Year of Plenty — take any 2 resources
Monopoly — claim all of one resource from every player

blocks.text: Unless a card says otherwise, it can't be played the same turn it was bought.
Rolling a 7 stops all production. Anyone holding more than 7 cards discards half, rounded down.
The active player moves the robber to any hex, blocking it, and may steal one random resource from an opponent touching that hex.
If the robber lands on your own settlement or city, you may pay 1 Lumber + 1 Brick + 1 Grain + 1 Wool + 1 Ore, once per turn, to send it straight to the Neutral Zone instead.
The Neutral Zone never produces resources and isn't considered anyone's territory.
Claim this once you've played at least 3 Knights and have more than any other player — worth 2 Victory Points.
Claiming it also advances the Season Track. Another player can take it over by playing more Knights than you.
Awarded to the player with the longest unbroken chain of 5 or more connected roads — worth 2 Victory Points.
An opponent's settlement or city breaks your chain, and another player can take the title with a longer network.
A Resort's exact point value depends on your game's implementation.
The host chooses a game mode in the lobby's Advanced Rules. A mode adds a twist on top of the normal rules; everything else you set still applies.

items: ⚡ Blitz — a fast game on a small board, first to 6 points
🃏 Draft — pick your starting resources and hexes in a card draft
🌊 Shrinking — the coastline floods and the map gets smaller

blocks.text: The mode is locked in when the lobby is created, and everyone can see it in the header during the game.
A short, sharp game. Blitz sets three rules for you:

items: 30-second action timer (your own timer setting can only make it shorter)

blocks.text: With less land to share, expansion gets tight quickly — settle fast and block your rivals early. Seasons and the other options work as usual.

Before building, everyone drafts. Each player is dealt a pack of 6 cards. Each round, every player picks one card from the pack in front of them at the same time, then passes the pack to the next seat.

items: 4 rounds — you end up with 4 cards
You only ever see the pack in front of you
Each card is either a Hex Claim or a Resource Bundle
If you are idle for 40 seconds, the best card is picked for you

blocks.text: When the draft ends, placement works as usual: two settlements and two roads each, in turn order.

items: Hex Claim — you claim that hex (marked with a flag in your colour). Whenever its number is rolled, you receive +1 of its resource, even with no building on it. The robber and flooding still block it.
Resource Bundle — 3 resource cards (a rare bundle gives 4), paid from the bank when the draft ends. If the bank runs short, you get what is left.

blocks.text: Draft replaces the bonus from the second settlement: you no longer collect resources for it — your drafted cards are your starting hand. The desert is never offered.
The sea is rising. After the 4th full round, and then every 4 rounds, the coastline floods inward: a few outer hexes go under at the end of the round.
Nothing is a surprise: the hexes that will flood next are marked with a red dashed outline and a 🌊, and the header counts down the rounds until the next tide.
About one hex in every nine on the board floods per tide (2 on the standard board). Only coastal hexes can flood, so the island shrinks from the outside in.

items: The robber cannot be placed on a flooded hex; if its hex floods, the robber is washed away until the next 7 or Knight
You cannot build a settlement on an intersection — or a road on an edge — that touches only flooded hexes
Buildings and roads you already own stay: they keep counting for points, Longest Road, and so on

blocks.text: Flooding stops when only 40% of the starting hexes (at least 6) remain. After that final tide, everyone plays one more round, and then the player with the most Victory Points wins. Ties: most cities and resorts, then settlements, then cards in hand. Reaching the point target before then still wins immediately.
You earn Gold for playing. It is only used to buy cosmetics in the Shop and never affects gameplay.

items: Game mode multiplier: Blitz ×0.75; Draft and Shrinking ×1.25
Matches against bots only pay half
Match income is capped at 300 Gold per day
Achievements give one-time bonuses — the full list is in the Shop

blocks.text: Rewards are paid once per match when it ends and are saved on this device.
Open the Shop from the main menu to spend your Gold on three kinds of cosmetics:

items: 🗺️ Board themes — change how the board looks, for you only
🏠 Piece skins — a new finish for your roads and buildings, seen by everyone (your colour never changes)
🖼️ Avatar frames — a ring around your avatar, seen by everyone

blocks.text: Buy an item once, then equip it from the Shop or your Inventory whenever you like. Items are purely cosmetic and cannot be traded.
Optional: instead of dice, you may use a number die or number wheel to determine the production number.
Either method still interacts with the Season system exactly as normal.
Optional: players can choose from different maps, each with its own terrain layout, number tokens, ports, and desert placement.
Whichever map is chosen stays active for the whole game.
Scaling the map keeps enough room to expand while still competing for good locations.
The game ends the instant a player reaches 10 or more Victory Points — that player wins immediately.
In Shrinking mode the game can also end after the final tide: the player with the most Victory Points wins (see Game Modes).
That's everything you need to know. Now go build, trade, scheme, and conquer.
Good luck and happy settling!

tutIntroParagraph: Reach {vp} Victory Points before anyone else and the island is yours. Points come from Settlements, Cities, Resorts, the Longest Road, and the Largest Army. This guide focuses on the hands-on mechanics — the ones you'll actually click, place, and roll. Pick a chapter below, or use the shelf on the left.
roadsLead: Roads connect your territory. Every road must touch one of your existing roads, Settlements, or Cities — you can't build in isolation.
roadsRuleCard: A road may never be built through another player's Settlement or City.
roadsTryIt: Try it: click any glowing edge on the map to lay your first road, then keep extending your network from there.
settlementsLead: Settlements come in two flavors depending on when you place them.
setupPlacementText: At the start of the game, your first two Settlements are free. The Distance Rule still applies — you can't place one right next to another Settlement or City. After your second Settlement, you collect starting resources from its adjacent tiles.
buildingPhaseText: Every Settlement after setup must be connected to one of your Roads and follow the Distance Rule.
citiesLead: A City is a Settlement that's leveled up — it replaces the Settlement on the same spot and produces double.
citiesCostCard: A Settlement produces 1 resource per roll; a City produces 2. Worth 2 Victory Points instead of 1.
citiesNeedSettlement: Need a Settlement to upgrade first. Head to Chapter II if your map doesn't have one of your own yet.
robberLead: Roll a 7 and the Robber wakes up: no tile produces that turn, players with more than 7 cards discard half, and you move the Robber onto a tile of your choice — blocking it and letting you steal a card from anyone settled there.
robberPeaceText: If the Robber lands on a tile where you have a Settlement or City, you may pay one of every resource, once per turn, to send it straight to the Neutral Zone.
seasonsLead: The Season Track shifts every 5 turns, or the moment someone claims the Largest Army. Each season bends how the dice behave.
seasonSpringRule: 🌸 Spring — Fertility: rolling 6 or 8 gives Fields & Pastures +1 extra resource.
seasonSummerRule: ☀️ Summer — Harvest: rolling 5 or 9 doubles that tile's production.
seasonAutumnRule: 🍂 Autumn — Abundance: Forests & Hills also produce on 3 and 11.
seasonWinterRule: ❄️ Winter — Hardship: rolling 2 or 12 skips production and costs you a random resource.
resortLead: A Resort lets you seize an opponent's City outright. Their City is removed, your Resort takes its place, and they lose the Victory Points that City was worth. A Resort can never be built over or replaced.
resortCostCard: Can only overtake a City — never a plain Settlement.
resortTryIt: The maroon marker on the map is a rival's City. Try taking it.
exitConfirmBody: You'll return to the main menu. Other players can continue without you.
boardEditorHint: Click a tile to cycle its terrain. Click the number to change it. You need exactly one Desert.

modeDesc_blitz: Fast game: smaller board, shorter turn timer, first to 6 victory points.
modeDesc_draft: Instead of the usual setup bonus, draft starting resources and claim hexes by passing packs, like a card draft.
modeDesc_shrinking: The coastline floods inward on a visible schedule. Fight over the land that remains — the last tide ends the game.

tideFinal: Final tide! The game ends in {n} turn(s) — most victory points wins.
tideEnded: The final tide ended the game — most victory points wins.
